title: PMOS: regions, sign conventions and small-signal use

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
A PMOS is an NMOS with every polarity reversed: a p-channel forms in an n-type body when the gate is pulled **below** the source, and holes flow from source to drain. The cleanest way to avoid sign errors is to write every PMOS quantity source-referenced and positive: \(V_{SG}\), \(V_{SD}\), \(|V_{Tp}|\) and \(|V_{ov}| = V_{SG} - |V_{Tp}|\). With those, the NMOS rules carry over word for word. The device is on when \(V_{SG} > |V_{Tp}|\), saturated when \(V_{SD} \ge |V_{ov}|\), and its current flows **out** of the drain.

For small signals the reader's advice is to "wiggle" the gate. Raising \(V_G\) lowers \(V_{SG}\), so the current falls. The PMOS model drawn upside down, with \(g_mv_{sg}\) from source to drain, is exactly the NMOS model with \(g_mv_{gs}\) from drain to source. \(g_m\) is always positive. A PMOS common-source stage, with its source at the supply (an AC ground), has the same gain formula as the NMOS stage and is still inverting. Electrons are more mobile than holes, so for the same size and current a PMOS has lower \(g_m\).

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ I_D = \tfrac12\mu_pC_{ox}\tfrac WL(V_{SG} - |V_{Tp}|)^2, \qquad V_{SD} \ge V_{SG} - |V_{Tp}| \iff V_D \le V_G + |V_{Tp}| \]
\[ i_{sd} = g_mv_{sg} + \frac{v_{sd}}{r_o}, \qquad A_v = -g_m(r_o\parallel R_D) \]

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A PMOS with its source at 3.3 V, \(|V_{Tp}| = 0.7\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(\mu_pC_{ox}W/L = 0.8\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\) has \(V_G = 2.1\ \mathrm{V}\). Then \(V_{SG} = 1.2\ \mathrm{V}\), \(|V_{ov}| = 0.5\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(I_D = \tfrac12(0.8)(0.25) = 0.1\ \mathrm{mA}\). The drain may rise to \(V_G + |V_{Tp}| = 2.8\ \mathrm{V}\) before the device leaves saturation.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Plugging negative \(V_{GS}\) and \(V_{Tp}\) into NMOS formulas and flipping inequalities by accident.
- Using a negative \(g_m\) for a PMOS and then also flipping the model.
- Thinking a PMOS stage is non-inverting because the device is "upside down".

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: PMOS devices make the current-source loads, mirror loads and level-shifting stages that appear in every later amplifier.
